title: Impact of nonlinear electrodynamics on quasinormal modes of rotating black strings
abstract: We study massless scalar perturbations of rotating anti-de Sitter black strings sourced by a power-Maxwell field with negative exponent $s$. The charge enters the metric function as $-Qr^{p}$ with $p=2/(1-2s)$, and the case $s=-1/2$ gives a linear term with an algebraic horizon. Since rotation is a local boost of the static string, the rotating spectrum follows exactly from the static one evaluated at a frequency-dependent momentum. We compute the spectrum with the Horowitz-Hubeny series, Chebyshev collocation and time-domain evolution, each implemented in two independent codes and checked against the planar Schwarzschild-AdS limit. The charge acts in two ways. At the reduced charge $\hat q_c=0.72626$ the least damped pair of modes meets on the imaginary axis, so more strongly charged strings ring down without oscillation, and at the endpoint of the branch the spectrum is exactly hypergeometric. At large transverse momentum the distance of the modes from the light cone grows as $k^{1/(1-4s)}$, replacing the $k^{-1/5}$ law of the neutral brane. Rotation continues the exceptional point into a line in the plane of charge and rotation, adds a purely damped axisymmetric tower, and never produces superradiant growth. A near-horizon estimate used earlier for this geometry misses all of these effects.
summary: This paper analyzes the quasinormal modes of rotating black strings modified by nonlinear electrodynamics. Using advanced numerical techniques, the authors demonstrate that the charge dictates whether the ringdown is oscillatory or purely damped, and that rotation introduces new spectral features like an exceptional line. The work highlights the necessity of considering boundary effects over simple near-horizon approximations.
main_problem: The study investigates how nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED) modifies the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of rotating black strings in an anti-de Sitter (AdS) background.
main_result: The charge significantly alters the ringdown behavior, causing overdamping at specific charge values, and the spectrum is governed by complex interplay between the horizon and near-boundary effects.
method: The authors employed three independent numerical techniques—Horowitz-Hubeny series, Chebyshev collocation, and time-domain evolution—to solve the radial wave equation.
model_or_system: The system is a rotating black string sourced by a power-Maxwell field, described by a metric function $f(r)$ derived from Einstein gravity coupled to NLED. Perturbations are analyzed via a scalar test field $\Psi$.
key_observables: Quasinormal mode frequencies ($\omega_n$), the exceptional point ($\hat{q}_c$), and the large transverse momentum law exponent.
important_parameters: The NLED charge ($\hat{q}$), the rotation parameter ($a/l$), and the negative exponent ($s$) of the power-Maxwell field.
main_assumptions: The rotating spectrum is assumed to follow exactly from the static one via a frequency-dependent momentum boost map, and the analysis confirms that simple near-horizon estimates are insufficient.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the static scalar spectrum showing mode movement toward the imaginary axis and collision at $\hat{q}_c$, and time-domain profiles comparing oscillatory ringdown at low charge versus purely damped tails at high charge.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing radial equation, relates the rotating spectrum to the static one via a boost map, calculates the spectrum using multiple numerical methods, and analyzes asymptotic behavior and the impact of charge and rotation.
why_interesting: While focused on general relativity, the analysis of damped oscillations (QNMs) and the study of exceptional points in parameter space are mathematically analogous to open quantum systems and quantum decay processes.
